question: Should editor exports and DOM contracts use neutral names across the Plate facade and its runtime, and which public nouns should disappear instead of being renamed?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, frozen from status at fe0e9599a6 on 2026-10-04 (39 units), and judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was open as pursue-unbound at queue position 25. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Public identifiers, observable DOM properties, persisted and clipboard formats, defaults and config knobs use neutral editor vocabulary (the accepted 'Ok go all' direction).
No compatibility aliases or legacy branded readers; prior branded formats are unsupported input (adoption plan precedent).
Package names, import specifiers and implementation filenames are not a brand-removal corpus.
Root VISION.md is the mandatory first read and wins conflicts (AGENTS.md:74), so it must name the live API.
Public JSDoc defaults must match runtime behavior.
Repair the mechanism that let the violation escape (AGENTS.md pokayoke rule).
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-13 closure audit and the 2026-09-12 adoption plan's mapping as historical evidence, then rechecked on the live tree editorSelection in proof.ts, the __EDITOR_* keys in @platejs/test, the absence of Plite in Plate JSDoc and public docs outside performance.mdx and the migration pages, the generated platejs API manifest (no branded names except the truthful MigratePlateV54 migration types) and local dist declarations without plitejs imports. Then searched quoted string literals and __-prefixed keys for plite and plate tokens across plitejs, platejs and @platejs/test source and dated each hit with git log -S.
summary: Job: Plate users learn one neutral editor vocabulary across exports, DOM, wire formats, defaults and teaching, with no compatibility aliases. Live source closes the 2026-09-13 residuals: @platejs/test exposes editorSelection, profiler, IME and trace globals use __EDITOR_*, Plate JSDoc and public docs are clean outside the approved exceptions, and the local Plate declaration build has no plitejs module reference. Five branded observable values remain, three added after the hard cut ('plate-comments' 2026-09-18, 'plite-plain-text' 2026-09-27, the public installBrowserHandle export 2026-10-03), plus the published @platejs/test knob PLITE_BROWSER_CLIPBOARD_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS and the plite-editor-N default id; root VISION.md still names <Plite decorations>, editor.extension(Extension).api, EditorExtensionTypeProvider, extension groups and toPlatePlugin(). Stop loses because these are public product, persisted and documented outputs rather than implementation identifiers, and the recurrence shows a missing guard; the direct hard cut plus a string-literal check is the smallest repair.

callSites.proposed: Proposed: installBrowserHandle() sets a neutral element key (for example __editorBrowserHandle) whose insertData takes { fragment }; createEditor().id follows a neutral documented default; toJSON() returns { kind: 'comments', version: 1, ... }; VISION.md teaches <EditorRoot decorations>, editor.plugin(Plugin).api, PluginTypeProvider and toReactPlugin().

reconciliation.reason: Public docs stay clean outside the approved exceptions.

alternatives: Keeping the values as implementation identifiers loses. installBrowserHandle is a documented platejs/react export, @platejs/test publishes with public access, CommentsJSON is a public persisted type and editor.id is public output.

Hard-cutting the five values and the root doctrine is selected. It brings a neutral browser-handle key and insertData field, a neutral comments kind, a neutral plain-text format key, a neutral default editor id that matches its JSDoc, a neutral clipboard-lock env var, and root VISION wording that matches plite.md and plate.md, with no aliases or old readers.

Adding a static check for plite and plate tokens in string literals of public package source, with an explicit allowlist (package names, import specifiers, the __PLATE_INSTANCES__ duplicate-package guard), is needed with the cut, because three of the five values arrived after the closure audit.
Dual-reading old values (accepting 'plate-comments' alongside the new kind) loses. It repeats the two-dialect cost the adoption rejected, and the beta does not support prior branded formats.
Renaming __PLATE_INSTANCES__ too loses. It counts duplicate platejs package copies and names the package truthfully.
proofLimits: Source, git history and local build inspection only; no tests, builds, browser or packed release. The string-literal search covered quoted plite/plate tokens and __-prefixed keys in plitejs, platejs and @platejs/test source; it is not an exhaustive census of every observable value (CSS-in-JS, generated registry payloads and templates were not scanned). packages/platejs/src/lib/editor/withPlite.ts has unstaged edits from another session; the cited lines also exist at HEAD. Changing CommentsJSON.kind and the default editor id changes saved or observable data; the deferred comments unit overlaps, and the persisted-format call should follow the adoption precedent that prior branded formats are unsupported. VISION.md:131 is also touched by the distribution Pursue.
